dream_growth.grows_from: the dark of the hedge burrow (LGT-field-hedge-burrow-01)
dream_growth.how: The eyelid glow of the fall is gone: overhead is the black of the burrow. The only light is lamp-glow from the long hall round the corner, the dream's amber stand-in for the afternoon sun, which gets warmer and brighter as she runs toward it.

schemes.key: warm lamp-glow spilling round the right-angle corner at the west end of the passage, from the long hall's oil lamps
schemes.direction_note: from the landing (east end) the light is ahead, at the far west end; figures running toward it are silhouetted with warm rims; overhead is always black

fill.note: the landing chamber and heap of sticks get only a faint, cool, near-black ambient; no light comes from the shaft opening

practicals: (off-frame) the long hall's oil lamps, seen only as glow on the corner reveal
schemes.atmosphere: cool still air; leaf-dust hanging after the landing, lit where it drifts into the glow
schemes.prompt_fragment_en: Near-darkness at the foot of the well: pitch black overhead, cool dim shadow over the heap of dry sticks and leaves, and the only light a warm amber lamp-glow spilling round the right-angle corner at the far end of the long, low passage, rim-lighting drifting dust and turning a running figure into a silhouette against it; hard contrast, hushed, expectant mood.
schemes.reason: 'All dark overhead' and the passage are explicit (ch001-p11), and the Rabbit must stay visible. The hall's lamps (ch001-p11) are the only named light, so their spill round the corner is used; architecture already marks the lit corner. S01 and S02 share one condition, so one scheme.
